english.title: Receiver of information from primary recipient disclose confidential information
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person who had obtained confidential information from **(..SPECIFY THE PRIMARY RECIPIENT..), disclosed it, in contravention of section 348 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, without

(A)_[the consent of the person from whom the primary recipient received the information]_
(B)_[the consent of **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) to whom it related]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 352(1) and (2) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 401 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that proceedings for offences may be instituted in England and Wales only by the Authority or the Secretary of State or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.
(ii) Section 352(6) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that in proceedings for an offence under this section it is a defence for the accused to prove:-
(a) that he did not know and had no reason to suspect that the information was confidential information or that it had been disclosed in accordance with section 350;
(b) that he took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid committing the offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
